title: Neutron star mergers are observed via gravitational waves and light.
narration: When two neutron stars collide in a distant galaxy, they send out ripples in spacetime called gravitational waves—and a brilliant flash of light. This extraordinary event, known as a kilonova, opens a new window for astronomers to study the cosmos using multiple messengers at once.
ssml: <speak>When two neutron stars collide in a distant galaxy, they send out ripples in spacetime called gravitational waves—and a brilliant flash of light.<break time="500ms"/> This extraordinary event, known as a kilonova, opens a new window for astronomers to study the cosmos using multiple messengers at once.</speak>

claims.text: When two neutron stars collide, they produce both gravitational waves and a flash of light.
A neutron star merger is called a kilonova and allows astronomers to observe the universe using multiple messengers.
